# FDG3048

> DO follow the guidelines described in Table 3-5 when naming types derived from or implementing certain .NET types.

Framework Design Guidelines, 3rd edition, section 3.5.2 Names of Common Types.

## How it is checked

- Check: sdk (partial coverage)
- Diagnostics: CA1710, CA1711
- Automatic fix: not applied automatically (the fix can break callers)
- Severity: library warning, application warning, test none
- Status: draft

By default (dotnet_code_quality.CA1710.exclude_indirect_base_types = true) CA1710 checks only the direct base type, so a type derived from a subclass, such as an exception derived from ArgumentException or a class derived from Dictionary<TKey, TValue>, is not reported (probe with SDK 10.0.402). Renaming a public type changes the public API, so the fix is breaking; CA1710 and CA1711 have no code fix.

## From the book

These suffixing guidelines apply to the whole hierarchy of the specified base type. For example, it is not just types derived directly from `System.Exception` that need the suffixes, but also those derived from `Exception` subclasses.

These suffixes should be reserved for the named types. Types derived from or implementing other types should not use these suffixes. For example, the following represent incorrect naming:

```csharp
public class ElementStream : Object { ... }
public class WindowsAttribute : Control { ... }
```
